nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: Commercial Ni foam was cut into 2.5×2.5 cm² plates, then compressed into thinner ones to improve the wettability. Ni foam was sequentially ultrasonically treated in 3M hydrochloric acid (HCl) aqueous solution, deionized water, and ethanol to remove the surface oxides and organic molecules, then dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C.

nodes.source_text: Before the synthetic procedures, commercial Ni foam was cut into 2.5×2.5 cm² plates... dried in a vacuum oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: First hydrothermal precursor formation
nodes.procedure: The clean Ni foam plate was immersed in 35 mL of a uniform transparent aqueous solution containing (NH4)2HPO4 (1 mM). Then, the sealed 50 mL autoclave was retained at 180°C for different times to prepare the precursors. The achieved green precursors were washed several times with deionized water and dried in air.

nodes.name: Second hydrothermal Ni(OH)2 formation
nodes.procedure: The green precursor was transformed into a 50 mL Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave containing 30 mL of 0.1 M KOH aqueous solution. Subsequently, the autoclave was kept at 120°C for 5 h. After cooling to room temperature, the light gray Ni(OH)2/NF nanoarrays were rinsed with deionized water and dried in air.

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal treatment
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the autoclave was kept at 120°C for 5 h

nodes.source_text: Then, another mild hydrothermal process was utilized... dried in air.

nodes.name: Phosphorization to Ni2P/NF
nodes.procedure: The freshly obtained Ni(OH)2/NF and NaH2PO2·H2O, with a weight ratio of 1:10, were put into the same ceramic boat at two separated places, while NaH2PO2·H2O is at the upstream side. After excluding air for 30 min in flowing Ar at room temperature, the samples were maintained at 300°C for 30 min with a heating rate of 5°C/min under a flowing Ar atmosphere. After naturally cooling to room temperature, the achieved black samples were collected for further tests.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the samples were maintained at 300°C for 30 min with a heating rate of 5°C/min under a flowing Ar atmosphere

nodes.source_text: The Ni2P/NF was prepared via a low-temperature calcination method... collected for further tests.

nodes.name: Ni-Fe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: Clean Ni foam was put into 30 mL of a transparent light green aqueous solution containing 0.5 mM Fe(NO3)2·9H2O, 0.5 mM Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 3 mM urea, and 7.5 mM NH4F. Then the 50 mL autoclave was transferred into an oven and kept at 120°C for 6 h. After cooling to room temperature, the obtained Ni-Fe LDH was rinsed with deionized water and dried in air.
nodes.source_text: The Ni-Fe LDH was synthesized with a modified reported method... dried in air for further use.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: Ni₂P/NF catalyst exhibits an excellent electrocatalytic activity... can sustain current densities of 1000 and 1500 mA cm⁻² at overpotentials of 306 and 368 mV... Tafel plots give slopes of 76 mV dec⁻¹ for Ni₂P/NF... C_dl of Ni₂P/NF (55.2 mF cm⁻²)... R_ct of Ni₂P/NF is 3.5 Ω

nodes.description: HER stability testing in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Multistep chronoamperometric curves were measured under a wide potential range (from 240 to 650 mV) and multistep chronopotentiometry curves were recorded across a broad current density (from 100 to 4000 mAcm⁻²). ... the long-term chronoamperometry (j-t) test shows that a high current density of 2500 mA cm⁻² can be maintained without decrease after 10 h

nodes.description: Overall water splitting (OWS) in 1 M KOH two-electrode system (Ni₂P||Ni-Fe LDH)
nodes.source_text: overall water splitting in a two-electrode system using 1 M KOH electrolyte... Ni₂P||Ni-Fe LDH... rapidly surpasses Pt/C||Ir/C at higher current densities (>600 mA cm⁻²)... Faradaic efficiency of ∼100%

nodes.description: OER performance characterization of Ni-Fe LDH
nodes.source_text: The Ni-Fe LDH catalyst has pure phase and outstanding OER property (Figures S27 to S29)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show uniform nanoarray morphology of Ni₂P/NF inherited from Ni(OH)₂ precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM and TEM images of the obtained Ni₂P show a uniform nanoarray morphology, inherited from the original Ni(OH)₂ precursor (Figures 1b-d and S9).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm nanowire diameter of ~250 nm for Ni(OH)₂/NF precursor.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images confirm the formation of nanowires with a diameter of ~250 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows distinct lattice fringes with spacing of 0.13 nm attributed to the (311) plane of hexagonal Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images demonstrate distinct lattice fringes with a spacing of 0.13 nm that could be attributed to the (311) plane of hexagonal Ni₂P.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm hexagonal Ni₂P phase consistent with HRTEM results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: which is consistent with the results from the XRD patterns (Figures 1e,f, S10, and S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDX mapping shows Ni and P uniformly distributed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX and XPS survey spectra verify the existence of Ni and P, which are uniformly distributed, as shown in our STEM elemental mapping.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peaks at 857.2 eV and 875.1 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂) and P 2p peak at 134.3 eV verify Ni₂P formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni 2p spectra analysis shows that the two obvious peaks at 857.2 and 875.1 eV can be attributed to Ni 2p₃/₂ and Ni 2p₁/₂. The peak at 134.3 eV originates from P 2p.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Ni₂P/NF is 3.5 Ω at 100 mV overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) Nyquist plots reveal that the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Ni₂P/NF is 3.5Ω which is much lower than that of Ni(OH)₂/NF (25.2Ω) and blank NF (69.5Ω) at an overpotential of 100mV

nodes.characterization_summary: CV gives double-layer capacitance C_dl of 55.2 mF/cm² indicating more exposed active sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl of Ni₂P/NF (55.2 mF cm⁻²) is larger than Ni(OH)₂/NF (3.1 mF cm⁻²) and blank NF (1.0 mF cm⁻²)
